title: SARS-CoV-2 Nucleocapsid Protein forms biomolecular condensates and interacts with ALS-associated RNA binding proteins in vitro
authors: Joseph-Patrick W.E. Clarke; Alexandra Keating; Veronica Noches; Crystal McLellan; Davide Dulcis; John Ravits; Michael J. Strong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究SARS-CoV-2核衣壳蛋白与ALS相关RNA结合蛋白的相分离凝聚体及TDP-43共定位，涉及蛋白-RNA互作但非TF-DNA体系，且无AI或物理模拟建模方法，仅湿实验，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: As we have entered the endemic phase of COVID-19, there is a need to assess the long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the trajectory of neurodegenerative disorders. Herein, we investigate whether the SARS-CoV-2 RNA-binding nucleocapsid protein (NCP; N-protein) may influence molecular processes relevant to motor neuron degeneration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). We detected N-protein immunoreactivity in ALS spinal cord motor neurons, including cytoplasmic N-protein-positive puncta that colocalized with cytoplasmic TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43). In vitro, optogenetically induced N-protein biomolecular condensates (BMCs) showed reversible, liquid-like behavior and recovered after photobleaching. Using this model, we found that these condensates colocalized with TDP-43 and the RNA-binding proteins G3BP1/2, PABPC1 and TIA1. Condensate formation was associated with TDP-43 cytoplasmic mislocalization, altered TARDBP expression, and altered exon 3 splicing of POLDIP3 . The N-terminal portion of N-protein influenced BMC formation, whereas truncated C-terminal proteoforms did not form detectable BMCs or show detectable TDP-43 colocalization in this assay. Extending these observations to a human cell model, we show that optogenetically induced N-protein BMCs colocalize with TDP-43 in human iPSC-derived motor neurons. Collectively, these findings support further investigation into potential molecular links between SARS-CoV-2 exposure and the trajectory of neurodegenerative disease.
abstract_zh: 随着我们进入COVID-19的地方性流行阶段，有必要评估SARS-CoV-2感染对神经退行性疾病轨迹的长期影响。在此，我们研究SARS-CoV-2 RNA结合核衣壳蛋白（NCP；N蛋白）是否可能影响与肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）中运动神经元变性相关的分子过程。我们在ALS脊髓运动神经元中检测到N蛋白免疫反应性，包括与细胞质TAR DNA结合蛋白43（TDP-43）共定位的细胞质N蛋白阳性点状结构。在体外，光遗传学诱导的N蛋白生物分子凝聚体（BMCs）表现出可逆的、液体样行为，并在光漂白后恢复。利用该模型，我们发现这些凝聚体与TDP-43及RNA结合蛋白G3BP1/2、PABPC1和TIA1共定位。凝聚体形成与TDP-43细胞质错定位、TARDBP表达改变以及POLDIP3外显子3剪接改变相关。N蛋白的N端部分影响BMC形成，而截短的C端蛋白形式在本检测中未形成可检测的BMCs或显示可检测的TDP-43共定位。将这些观察扩展到人类细胞模型，我们显示光遗传学诱导的N蛋白BMCs在人类iPSC来源的运动神经元中与TDP-43共定位。总体而言，这些发现支持进一步研究SARS-CoV-2暴露与神经退行性疾病轨迹之间潜在的分子联系。
